behaviorDesc: Grazes in the open at dawn and dusk, always with one ear on the treeline. A stag will stand between you and the herd — and a stag in the rut answers a challenge.
description: a big russet deer, the stag carrying a wide crown of antlers
diseaseVector: Deer carry ticks — check the hide before you carry it. Cook the meat through.
huntText: The herd lifts its heads as one. The stag steps forward, antlers wide — deciding whether you're worth the trouble.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — a mountain of venison, and a hide worth tanning. The antlers are tools, trade, and trophy all at once.

knowledgeLevels.1: Red deer. Big russet deer; stags carry wide antlers.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (excellent, lean), hide (large), antlers (tools), bones (needles, awls). Gut fast, hang high.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: the forest's main meat crop. Lean like all venison — eat with fat. The rut (fall) makes stags bold and dangerous.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: hunt the dawn meadows, wind in your face. In the rut, stags answer a bellow — call, don't chase. Never get between a stag and his hinds.

name: Red Deer
tell: freezes mid-step, head high, ears rotating like dishes.
unknown: something large and russet moving through the meadow mist

behaviorDesc: Sits tight in its form until the last second, then explodes in a zigzag. Hares outrun everything except a dog or a snare they don't see.
description: a big long-legged hare, ears laid flat, sitting tight in the grass
diseaseVector: Hares carry tularemia like rabbits — gloves for gutting, cook through.
huntText: It sits. You take one more step — and it's gone, a brown streak bouncing impossibly high.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — lean hare, a solid meal. Like rabbit: all protein, no fat — eat with something greasy.

knowledgeLevels.1: European hare. Big, long-legged, ears like antennae.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (lean), fur (soft, thin). Snare the runs between feeding grounds.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: protein — but lean (rabbit starvation applies). Best in the cold months when they're fat.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: find the forms (flattened grass nests) by day, snare by night. Hares run a circuit — learn it.

name: European Hare
tell: one ear swivels toward you; the body goes utterly still.
unknown: a brown shape that wasn't there a second ago

behaviorDesc: Scratches in coveys along field edges. Roosts in trees at night — a loud explosive flush when startled that warns everything for a mile.
description: a gaudy long-tailed game bird, the cock iridescent copper-green
diseaseVector: Wild birds can carry mites — pluck away from camp.
huntText: The covey erupts under your feet — wings hammering, cocks screaming. Pick one and commit.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — rich dark meat, and tail feathers worth keeping for fletching and trade.

knowledgeLevels.1: Pheasant. Gaudy long-tailed bird; the cock shines copper-green.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (dark, rich), feathers (fletching, trade). Roosts in trees — catch them going up at dusk.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: the field-edge meat bird. Hens are drabber and better eating (cocks are stringy in spring).
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: walk the field edges at last light toward the roost trees. A snare on the dust-bathing hollows works while you sleep.

name: Common Pheasant
tell: a harsh grating cackle from the hedge — then silence.
unknown: an explosion of wings and a gaudy flash of copper

behaviorDesc: Snuffles through leaf litter after dark, loud as a tiny pig. Rolls into a spiny ball when scared — patience beats force.
description: a spiny shuffling ball of a mammal, snuffling through the leaf litter
diseaseVector: Hedgehogs carry ticks and fleas — handle with gloves, cook well.
huntText: Snuffle, snuffle, pause. It hears you — and becomes a ball of spines. Wait it out or take it as it is.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — small but fatty. Bake it in clay, spines and all; the old way works.

knowledgeLevels.1: Hedgehog. A walking pincushion that snuffles.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (fatty for its size). The classic bake: clay-coat the whole animal, fire it, crack it open — spines come away with the clay.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: a fat little package — good when bigger game won't show. Mostly active after dark.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: listen for the snuffling after dusk along hedgerows. They hibernate in winter — don't dig them up; let them sleep.

name: European Hedgehog
tell: loud snuffling in the leaf litter, then sudden silence.
unknown: rustling in the leaves, like a tiny drunk pig

behaviorDesc: Digs setts that last centuries and defends them. Mostly wants earthworms, but cornered it fights like something three times its size.
description: a heavy black-and-white striped mammal, low-slung and purposeful
diseaseVector: Badgers can carry bovine TB — gloves, and cook the meat thoroughly.
huntText: It turns sideways — making itself wide, striped face low. That jaw can crush bone. Are you sure?
killText: About {kcal} kcal — strong dark meat, and a striped hide. Respect the animal; it died hard.

knowledgeLevels.1: Badger. Heavy, striped, low to the ground.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (strong-flavored, fatty), hide (tough). Trap the sett paths — never dig a sett.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: a serious meat package when the snares are lucky. Nocturnal; the paths to the sett are highways.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: setts are ancient — the same families for generations. Take the dispersing young in fall, never the breeding sow. And never corner one.

name: Eurasian Badger
tell: a low churring growl from the dark under the bushes.
unknown: a striped shadow digging with great serious purpose

behaviorDesc: Lives in the beech canopy, fattening on mast all fall. In a mast year they're everywhere; in a lean year they're ghosts.
description: a big sleepy gray dormouse, fat as a plum in the fall
diseaseVector: Dormice are clean as rodents go — still, cook them.
huntText: It blinks at you from the branch, too fat to hurry. The Romans kept these in jars and ate them with honey.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — tiny, but in fall it's a ball of nut-fat. A handful of them is a meal.

knowledgeLevels.1: Edible dormouse. A big fat gray dormouse, sleepy in the hand.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: the whole tiny animal — mostly fat in a mast year. The Romans fattened them on purpose; the name is literal.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: fall fat. When beech mast is heavy, dormice are heavy too — trap the runways.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: nest boxes and hollow branches. They hibernate half the year — take them in the fat weeks of October, never from a winter nest.

name: Edible Dormouse
tell: a soft chittering from the canopy at dusk.
unknown: a plump gray shape asleep on a branch

behaviorDesc: Grazes damp leaves after rain. Withdraws into its shell at a touch — collect by hand, no chase needed.
description: big spiral-shelled snails grazing the damp leaf litter
diseaseVector: Snails can carry rat lungworm — purge and cook thoroughly, never eat raw.
huntText: They don't flee. They barely hurry. Fill your bag.
killText: About {kcal} kcal per handful — chewy, mild, real food. Purge them on clean greens first, then cook.

knowledgeLevels.1: Edible snail. Big spiral shells in the damp.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: the meat from the shell. Purge 2-3 days on clean food, then boil or grill — never raw.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: slow but certain protein after rain. The old escargot animal — people paid for these.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: hunt after rain on limestone and old walls. Take the big ones, leave the small to grow.

name: Roman Snail
tell: silver trails on the wet leaves in the morning.
unknown: glossy spirals in the wet leaf litter

behaviorDesc: Ranges miles in a pack, testing everything. A missed strike answers itself — the pack investigates the shooter.
description: a big gray wolf, yellow-eyed, watching you the way you watch deer
diseaseVector: Wolves carry ticks and tapeworm — gloves for the hide, cook the meat.
huntText: It doesn't run. It watches. The pack is somewhere behind it, and now they know your smell.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — lean wolf, and a gray hide worth more than the meat. The pack will remember this.

knowledgeLevels.1: Gray wolf. Big, gray, yellow-eyed. The forest's old landlord.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (lean, strong), hide (prime). A predator answers a missed strike — the pack comes to investigate.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: dangerous game. Take lone dispersers, never the pack's core. Fire keeps them honest.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: they're smartest in winter when they're hungriest. Never turn your back on a pack that's decided you're interesting.

name: Gray Wolf
tell: a silence falls over the birds — then a howl, far off, answered nearer.
unknown: yellow eyes at the treeline, there and gone

behaviorDesc: Hangs motionless in the weeds, then strikes like a thrown spear. The freshwater shark — everything smaller is food.
description: a long torpedo of a fish hanging in the weeds, all teeth
diseaseVector: Raw freshwater fish can carry parasites. Cook it.
huntText: A shadow detaches from the weeds — long, green, patient. It watched your lure the way you watch it.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — firm white pike, excellent eating. Watch the Y-bones; they're the tax on the meal.

knowledgeLevels.1: Northern pike. Long, toothy, green — the creek's shark.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: big white fillets. Mind the Y-bones. A wire leader or it bites your line off.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: the best eating of the still waters. Ambush predator — fish the weed edges at dawn.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: big spoons, slow retrieve past the weed beds. In winter they go deep and sluggish — fish the holes.

name: Northern Pike
tell: a swirl in the shallows where no wind reached.
unknown: a green torpedo holding station in the current

behaviorDesc: Schools in the shallows, spiny dorsal cocked. Nips at anything — easy to catch, prickly to handle.
description: a striped little fish with a spiny sail of a dorsal fin
diseaseVector: Raw freshwater fish can carry parasites. Cook it.
huntText: The shallows boil with stripes — a school of perch, bold as brass, nipping at your hook.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — sweet white perch, worth the pricked thumbs. The spiny dorsal is the price of admission.

knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: small sweet fillets. Grip behind the gills — the dorsal spines mean business.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: the reliable pan fish. Where there's one there's twenty.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: dawn and dusk in the shallows. Small hooks, worms, patience.

name: European Perch
tell: a flurry of small splashes in the shallows.
unknown: striped flashes schooling in the shallows

behaviorDesc: Holds in the current behind stones, rising to the fly. Wild trout are wary — one wrong shadow and the pool empties.
description: a spotted bronze fish holding in the current
diseaseVector: Raw freshwater fish can carry parasites. Cook it.
huntText: A bronze flank turns in the current — spotted, perfect, and already watching your shadow.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — the prince of the creek, pink-fleshed and rich. Worth every cold hour.

knowledgeLevels.1: Brown trout. Bronze, black-and-red spotted, holding in the current.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: rich pink flesh. Fish upstream, keep your shadow off the water.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: the creek's prize. Needs clean cold water — where trout live, the water's drinkable (boil it anyway).
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: dawn, small flies or worms drifted natural. The big ones feed at last light under the banks.

name: Brown Trout
tell: a rise-ring spreading on the pool's surface.
unknown: a bronze shadow holding against the current
